# Unsupported run-child recovery

Six original DOCX packages are generated by
`tools/unknown_run_child_recovery_fixture.py`, using the project's original
mixed-picture XML and artwork helpers. No corpus or third-party artwork is
included. Each pair places ruby before, after, or on both sides of a supported
picture in the same bold, colored hyperlink run. The construct occurs in the
body, a table cell, the header and the footer; healthy neighboring runs and
numbering remain in the document.

ECMA-376 Part 1 (2016) §§17.3.3.24–27 describes the guide, base text and their
relative positioning. `unsupported` packages contain schema-valid `w:ruby`.
`matched` packages replace only that child with ordinary inline `readingBASE`
text: this is the explicit preview approximation, not the reference application's ruby layout.
Both kinds pass the official local transitional schema checks (30 views).

At `d5556227`, the three source pairs reproduce enclosing-run/hyperlink
rollback: the preview loses all four pictures and their links/formatting.
The regression also demonstrates the same boundary using an intentionally
unknown extension (a unit-only malformed input, not a conformance fixture).

Recovery now projects only the unrecognized child's visible text. Supported
neighboring text, pictures, hyperlink destinations and formatting use the
normal reader. The document stays read-only, the banner identifies the child
and source part and warns about the approximation, and download returns the
original bytes. No approximate export handler is attached.

The new branch does not catch errors from known readers or field parsing.
Those can have already changed state and need their own safe boundaries.
Nested formatting/objects inside the unknown child can still be omitted;
the disclosure explicitly warns that layout may differ. Full ruby positioning,
editing and selection remain open in T02, and R01–R06 remain open.

Tests compare supported structure and full-page pixels/geometry with the matched
approximation at 75% and 100%, exercise read-only input and original download,
and verify that field instructions/deleted text are not exposed. There is no
native reference equivalence claim for the approximation. A source scan of all 368
corpus files found no ruby elements in their word XML parts; this generic recovery
fix does not promote a corpus entry. Counts remain 210 complete / 158 partial.

Local verification: 54 unit tests, six browser tests, 30 schema views, production
build and license checks passed. Unit checks used one worker and a 30-second
diagnostic timeout; browser deadlines were unchanged. Full-page comparisons
and source hashes were checked during that verification.
The build's existing bundle-size warning remains an optimization note.
